[BURSEVI:v7p53/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · ضحاك | reports | A report in al-Muwaḍḍiḥ says God set nineteen mountains as pegs so the earth would stand, naming Qāf, Abū Qubays, Jūdī, Lebanon, and Sinai.
[BURSEVI:v7p53/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Some reports count more mountains than al-Muwaḍḍiḥ does, as Bursevī discussed under Sūrat al-Ḥijr.
[BURSEVI:v7p53/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعضهم | reports | Some say mountains are the bones and veins of the earth.
[BURSEVI:v7p53/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · أهل السلوك | reports | A Sufi cosmology makes sun and moon the eyes of this manifestation and stars reflected lights in its subtle veins, known by unveiling rather than philosophy.
[BURSEVI:v7p53/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God spread many kinds of animals through the earth, with abundant numbers and diverse genera.
[BURSEVI:v7p53/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Bathth means stirring up and scattering, like wind scattering dust or a soul disclosing its grief and evil.
[BURSEVI:v7p53/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The spreading of creatures points to God bringing into existence what was absent and making it manifest.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The description is evidence of God's power, wisdom, and workmanship; it lays groundwork for monotheism and refutes and rebukes idolatry.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The verse does not limit the wisdom of mountains to preventing sway; they have innumerable other purposes.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r11] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The author accepts a spherical earth, as held by al-Ghazali, and notes Ibn Abbas's report and philosophers' agreement; sense and inference support it.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | عمد is the plural of عماد, like أهب is the plural of إهاب; it means supports, and the plural reflects the multiple heavens.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | ترونها is an independent clause showing that if the heavens had supports, they would be visible; vision is visual, not intellectual.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively ترونها qualifies supports: the heavens have invisible pillars, interpreted as pillars of divine power; this interpretation is reported from Mujahid.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · مجاهد | reports | The interpretation of unseen supports is reported from Mujahid.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | The claim that a perfect human in each age supports the heavens, which fold when humanity ends, has no basis in Quran or Sunna.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | God placed lofty or firmly fixed mountains so the earth would not sway; without them surrounding waters and necessary storm winds might make it shift.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Some philosophers argue that on a spherical earth centered at the world's center of gravity, moving heavy objects could shift its center and move the earth, though imperceptibly because their mass is negligible.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another suggestion is that without mountains, a large sea formed by flowing water and windblown sand and soil could shift the earth.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | The verse does not prove that the heavens are immobile, as followers of Pythagoras say; other doctrines behind that view are even more plainly false.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | بث means bringing into existence and spreading; its root sense is stirring and dispersing, as in the images of scattered dust and dispersed moths. | mentions 56:6, 101:4
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The phrase means every kind or species of animal.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The water is rain and heaven means the upper direction; it may mean the canopy by figurative interpretation, but that should not be adopted without compelling evidence against observation.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Plants grow because of the rain; زوج means kind and كريم means noble or highly beneficial.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The shift to the first-person plural in both verbs highlights care: rain and growth recur and sustain animal life and the inhabited earth.
[ELMALILI:31:10-11/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | For “without pillars you see them,” Elmalılı directs readers to his commentary on 13:2. | mentions 13:2
[ELMALILI:31:10-11/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The verse establishes God's majesty and wisdom to prepare the affirmation of oneness; the shift to first-person speech in “We sent down” and “We gave” serves this purpose.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | Conditionally, if Quraysh’s question about Luqman and his son occasioned the surah, these verses through 31:12 introduce the story’s knowledge, wisdom, and guidance for believers; the question thus benefited them. | mentions 31:12
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | God’s creation is evidence against those who reject His signs: as creator of all creatures, He alone deserves divinity; assigning it to what creates nothing explains their rejection of the wise Book.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Treating idols as comparable to God in attributes implies denying divine wisdom, since wisdom is absent from the idols.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The argument is ‘proof of proof’ (tadqīq): it presents a thing with its evidence and the evidence for that evidence.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The direct address in ترونها and بكم is directed to the polytheists.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The phrase means ‘for fear that the earth sway beneath you’ or ‘so it does not sway you,’ as explained in the earlier parallel. | mentions 16:15

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The signs also embed favors: animals supply food, milk, wool, hides and transport; plants supply grain, fruit, fodder and truffles; sea creatures benefit people too. Creation thus displays both wisdom and mercy.
